title: The write guards the build declared closed as a class (O-044, ExplorerSettingsWriteCorpus.json) let through an ordinary writable open of Explorer\Advanced.
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: observed: FAIL B30 fires in the src guard (fitness.yaml src entry), 0 hit(s): using var key = Registry.CurrentUser.OpenSubKey(@"Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced", RegistryRights.SetValue);

C1: The src guard's OpenSubKey pattern (fitness.yaml src entry 'TheAppNeverWritesExplorersSettings (*.cs)') counts RegistryRights.SetValue/WriteKey/FullControl/CreateSubKey (`.` or `]::`) as writable: missing
C2: The xUnit twin ArchitectureRulesTests.TheAppNeverWritesExplorersSettings carries the same widened pattern, and eng/rules-parity.ps1 still says AGREE: missing

C3: Rule C ('no window case or hook changes Explorer's view settings', over tests/window/**) counts the PowerShell spelling [System.Security.AccessControl.RegistryRights]::SetValue as writable: missing

C4: Corpus rows B30 (src fire, RegistryRights.SetValue), B31 (src fire, Default plus FullControl), B32 (src quiet, ReadKey) and W35 (window fire, [RegistryRights]::SetValue) are in tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ExplorerSettingsWriteCorpus.json and pass: missing

C5: The class is closed as a class: a committed corpus with an inputs table, fire/quiet rows, an alias list and a census of every type that carries the value, bounded by who produces its members, with the before-fix code shown failing the rows it closes (answered by a `corpus` path): partial
C6: rules-parity and rules-harness --only for the touched plants pass after the change, with OpenSubKey RegistryRights plants recorded: partial

reg-import-and-reg-content-patterns: needs first: Fitness (taad_v3 backend/taad3/fitness.py:445) must decode a file that starts with FF FE or FE FF as UTF-16 before matching. Only then can rule C see W53 and W54 in the `.reg` file `reg export` writes. Nothing in tests/window/** needs this today.

W58 (`reg add $adv /v Hidden`): the practice proposal pinned it as miss; this composition fires it through a /v alternative in rule C's add branch, to match :1125's -Name-wherever-the-path-is-held rule.

The delete names use the prefix `RegDelete|SHDelete` with \w* (a superset, in the existing RegSetValue\w* style), where the spike measured the exact names `(RegDeleteValue|RegDeleteKeyValue|SHDeleteValue)[AW]?\b`.

`reg delete` and `reg import` fire whatever key they name, which is a conservative false positive on unrelated keys. The alternative is to require Explorer\Advanced on the line, which would miss an import of a .reg file.
The census and alias list live as top-level keys in the existing corpus file rather than in a separate census file.
CreateSubKey is dropped from the marker, per the measurement, instead of being kept as a conservative fire to match the brief and C1's wording.
The Remove-Item alias tokens (ri, rm, del, erase, rd, rmdir) on a line naming Explorer\Advanced are a bare-word tripwire that a future read line could trip.
Review m3 (waived, SC-308): no assertion in TheCorpusHoldsRows... that the census/aliases ids exist with the stated verdicts. Checked once at build time by a throwaway script instead.
Review m4 (waived, SC-309): no miss rows for rights held in a variable, a `using` alias of RegistryRights, or a split parent/child key path; bounded_by.not_pinned says so.
Review m5 (waived, SC-310): no multi-line plant in the repo's real layout.
.reg file content patterns: Fitness reads UTF-16LE as UTF-8 (risk spike no-go), so W53 and W54 are pinned as miss; the engine change is filed.
No semantic (AST or Roslyn) checker and no new architecture_rules, as the design decided.
If the class reopens, replace regex widening with a spelling-independent check: a PowerShell AST check for tests/window and a symbol-level banned-API check for src (#400).
Make taad_v3 Fitness (backend/taad3/fitness.py content_hits) decode a file starting FF FE or FE FF as UTF-16, then rule C could fire W53/W54 on .reg content.
docs/design/SL-091-hidden-reveal-refuses.md still describes these guards as closed as a class; reword it to 'bounded by producer' when next touched.
reg delete and reg import fire whatever key they name (a conservative false positive on unrelated keys, accepted in the design); revisit if a window script ever needs one.

deviation: The before-fix failing set is 42 ids, not the design's 33: the 33 plus B50 (DeleteSubKey row I added so the DeleteSubKey alternative is pinned on its own) and W60-W67 (W60 flipped miss to fire, W61-W64 and W65-W67 added) from the accepted review findings M1 and M2. Design said 46 rows; 61 were added: B30-B51, W35-W73 (also quiet controls B51, W68, W71, W72, W73 and miss rows W69, W70).

deviation: CreateSubKey is dropped from the rights marker, as the design decided; the issue text and build-check C1 name it, and C1's literal wording is therefore not met for that one word. The Sandbox measured RegSetValueExW returning 5 on such a handle, so B38 is a quiet row.
deviation: Review m1 changed the design's alias handling: the six Remove-Item aliases were not added (full cmdlet names only), with rm/sp pinned as miss rows.
deviation: The design said ExplorerSettingsWriteRuleTests is unchanged; I edited only its doc comments (the word 'closed' contradicted the 'bounded by producer' wording, #400).

deviation: The review-accepted rows and top-level keys use `closed_by` as a top-level key rather than a per-row field; plants.json's _note row counts and id lists were updated by hand to stay true (123 rows).

drift: Nothing departed from the design without being declared: - W60 moved from miss to fire, with W61-W67 and plants S56/S57 added, per accepted M1/M2. - The bare aliases were dropped per m1. - closed_by was added per m2. - Doc comments in ExplorerSettingsWriteRuleTests.cs were reworded. - CreateSubKey was dropped from the marker. The build declared each of these.

drift: docs/design/SL-091-hidden-reveal-refuses.md still describes both guards as 'closed as a class'. The corpus and both `because` texts now say 'bounded by producer'. This is declared as a follow-up but not done.
drift: Nothing new departed from the design without being declared. Round 1's drift notes stand.

not reached: An ordinary user's own HKCU\…\Explorer\Advanced. The Sandbox ran as SYSTEM. Key-level deletes and recreates (Remove-Item, DeleteSubKeyTree, New-Item -Force, Rename-Item, Move-Item) were refused on SYSTEM's real key for an unpinned reason, so they were measured on a scratch key of the same shape. The guard verdicts do not depend on this.

not reached: The effective Explorer setting (SHGetSetSettings or a fresh Explorer window) after each Sandbox write was not re-read. Only the registry values were. The investigation's earlier showAll 1→0 measurement covers only deleting Hidden.

not reached: Run-time behaviour under pwsh 7, which the window scripts may run under. The Sandbox has only Windows PowerShell 5.1. The investigation's round 1 measured the same handle behaviour on pwsh 7.6 / .NET 10.0.12.
not reached: Windows 10. Every measurement was on Windows 11 (host 26200, Sandbox 26100).
not reached: A rule hit in the repo's real multi-line layout: plants and rows are one line each (waived, SC-310).
not reached: Fitness on a UTF-16LE .reg file's content (W53, W54). That needs the taad_v3 engine to decode UTF-16, which is outside this repo.
not reached: Whether a managed key.SetValue after a RegistryRights open becomes a real write once dotnet/runtime#113535 ships. No runtime carries it.
criterion not met: Issue text: widen the marker to include CreateSubKey

critique missed: The critique named registry-provider cmdlets in M1 but enumerated only the verbs it had seen (New/Clear-Item, Copy/Move/Rename-ItemProperty). It never listed Get-Command -Module Microsoft.PowerShell.Management for *-Item and *-ItemProperty. Rename-Item, Move-Item and Rename-ItemProperty -Name HiddenOld -NewName Hidden therefore passed rule C. The existing :1125 `-Name` handling cannot see -NewName, and the lookaround group at :1124 does not list Rename-Item or Move-Item. Check to write: every verb of the provider cmdlet module has a fire, miss or out row in the census.

critique missed: The reg.exe census listed only add, delete and import. It was never checked against the `reg /?` verb list (query, add, delete, copy, save, restore, load, unload, compare, export, import, flags). `reg copy <backup> <Explorer\Advanced> /s /f` works unelevated on HKCU and writes Hidden back, but rule C's :1126 gets 0 hits.

critique missed: When M1 added New-Item to rule C, the critique asked only about the form with Explorer\Advanced adjacent on the line. It did not ask for the documented -Path <parent> -Name 'Advanced' -Force spelling, which recreates the key empty exactly as W60 does. :1124 needs adjacency, so the line gets 0 hits. Check to write: for each cmdlet added to a path-adjacency pattern, feed the -Path/-Name split spelling.

critique missed: The critique checked argument spellings of the OpenSubKey call but not how reg.exe is launched. This repo launches native programs through Start-Process -ArgumentList and ArgumentList.Add (WindowCases.ps1:473, :685, :5743). `Start-Process reg.exe -ArgumentList 'import',$file` and `& reg @('add',$adv,'/v','Hidden',...)` get 0 hits from :1126, which needs whitespace and the verb right after `reg`.

critique missed: The critique and design fired named-argument opens (B08 `writable: true`, B37 `rights: RegistryRights.SetValue`) but did not ask the same question of the value-name patterns. `key.DeleteValue(name: "Hidden")` and `key.SetValue(name: "Hidden", value: 1)` get 0 hits, because the src patterns need the quote directly after `(`. The bound was inconsistent and unpinned.

still unknown: Can an ordinary user's own HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced be removed, renamed, moved or recreated by Remove-Item, Rename-Item, Move-Item or New-Item -Force? SYSTEM's key refused all of them for an unpinned reason and only a scratch key was measured. That decides whether the key-level rows (W49, W50, W60 and the SC-313/SC-315 shapes) are real members for the producer.

still unknown: Does PowerShell 7 bind a quoted string second argument to OpenSubKey(string, bool) as $true, like Windows PowerShell 5.1? W36, W37, W38 and W46 (fire rows) were measured writable only on 5.1. Round 1 measured identical handle behaviour on pwsh 7.6 / .NET 10.0.12, but not the string-to-bool overload binding.

still unknown: Will the taad_v3 Fitness engine ever decode UTF-16 by BOM (fitness.py:445)? Until it does, W53 and W54 stay miss rows and no .reg-content pattern can be adopted. The change lives outside this repo.

still unknown: After a provider-cmdlet or reg.exe write other than deleting Hidden, does Explorer's effective setting change in a fresh process (SHGetSetSettings)? Only the deleted-Hidden case was read (showAll 1 to 0). The other write members were verified at the registry-value level only.

went wrong: Build-check halted on its first pass because a premise criterion ('the bug is present today') came back present and made the whole survey read `partial`. The second pass 'built anyway' with no new information, so the lap was wasted.

went wrong: O-017 was discharged as 'closed as the class registry-provider cmdlets'. Code review then found Rename-Item, Move-Item, Rename-ItemProperty -NewName and (second round) New-Item -Path <parent> -Name Advanced getting 0 hits. This is the failure lessons #225 and #400 warned about, and it happened with both handed in. Each review round fixed the verbs it named and left the next sibling.

went wrong: Five code-review findings were waived to the backlog as minor (O-024 to O-028: SC-311, SC-312, SC-313, SC-314, SC-315). Validate then measured O-024, O-025, O-026 and O-028 as real writes in the Sandbox. The slice passed while its own validation recorded known producer-made holes in a guard the corpus describes as 'bounded by producer'.

went wrong: The corpus's bounded_by.member names moving, renaming and copying as members, but neither the rows nor the census covered them. The build wrote that text without checking it against the rows, and only code review caught the contradiction.

went wrong: The design's expected failing-id set (33 ids, 46 rows) was wrong by the end: 42 ids, 61 rows. The design froze counts before the critique's accepted M1/M2 findings added B50 and W60-W67. The build declared this, but the design's 'exactly 33' check could not have held.

went wrong: Fixes the slice declared as follow-ups were not done: docs/design/SL-091-hidden-reveal-refuses.md still calls both guards 'closed as a class', contradicting the corpus and both `because` texts.

went wrong: The issue text asked for CreateSubKey in the marker and the build-check named it (C1). The measurement showed it cannot write, and the build dropped it. Validate recorded 'criterion not met' while passing the slice, with no recorded decision from a person on the deviation.
went wrong: All 12 findings were disposed of by a model, and critique-review was skipped by sizing without an account. The gates' precision on this slice is unmeasured.
